rounds.text: Kemistar Corporation Ltd is demonstrating explosive top-line and bottom-line acceleration, evidenced by a 96% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16], quarterly sales surging 252% year-over-year [E55], and net profit jumping 127% year-over-year [E57]. This operational momentum is supported by an increasing quarterly operating margin trend over the last four quarters [E30] and strong cash conversion, with operating cash flow reaching 1.82 times reported profit and fully backing earnings in March 2026 [E31]. Furthermore, the company benefits from a favorable macro backdrop with the chemicals sector residing firmly in a tailwind with a score of +0.70 [E64], alongside high promoter skin-in-the-game at 74.88% [E39] and a significant capital expenditure pipeline with Capital Work in Progress standing at ₹ 9.6 Cr [E38]. Working capital efficiency is also improving, as working capital requirements have successfully dropped from 23.9 days to 14.8 days [E49]. Conceded: the stock trades at an elevated P/E ratio of 71.3x alongside a negative free cash flow of ₹ -0.33 Cr [E1, E33].

Kemistar Corporation Ltd trades at a severe valuation disconnect, highlighted by a lofty price-to-earnings ratio of 71.3x against a sector benchmark of 21.32x [E1, E6]. This rich pricing is entirely detached from the company's weak fundamental profitability, evidenced by a low return on equity of 2.8% and a 5-year median ROE of just 4% [E13, E24]. Operating performance further undermines the bull thesis, with operating margins dropping by 7 percentage points to 5% in the trailing twelve months compared to three years prior [E27]. Moreover, the intrinsic valuation picture is deeply negative, with a discounted cash flow model placing value at Rs 11 per share against the market price of Rs 45.8, resulting in a margin of safety of -310.0% [E41, E42]. Operational friction is compounding these risks as debtor days have deteriorated significantly from 77.0 to 116 days [E53], and capital intensity is rising with borrowings increasing to Rs 9.32 Cr alongside negative free cash flow of Rs -0.33 Cr [E33, E37]. conceded: [E16]

The bear's focus on the 71.3x P/E ratio [E1] misses the explosive top-line acceleration currently underway, characterized by a 96% compounded sales growth rate over the trailing twelve months and quarterly sales leaping 252% year-over-year [E16, E55]. This rapid expansion is backed by high-quality execution, as profits are fully backed by cash with a cash conversion ratio of 1.82x for March 2026 and operating cash flow reaching 95% of operating profit [E31, E34]. Furthermore, the company's operating margin profile shows clear sequential momentum, reading increasing over the last four quarters [E30], while working capital requirements have efficiently compressed from 23.9 days down to 14.8 days [E49]. The macro backdrop strongly supports this operational pivot, operating inside a chemicals sector tailwind score of +0.70 to +0.73 [E62, E64] while maintaining a high dividend payout of 64.6% [E48]. conceded: [E13, E27, E41, E53]

The bull highlights explosive top-line acceleration through a 96% TTM sales growth and a 252% quarterly surge [E16, E55], but this massive revenue expansion fails to translate into acceptable capital returns, with ROE languishing at 2.8% [E13] and ROCE sitting at a meager 3.34% against a sector benchmark of 10.29% [E10]. While the bull points to strong cash conversion of 1.82x [E31], it glosses over the resulting negative free cash flow of Rs -0.33 Cr in March 2026 [E33] and rising borrowings that climbed to Rs 9.32 Cr from Rs 8.09 Cr a year earlier [E37]. The claim of sequential margin momentum [E30] is directly undercut by a compressed operating margin of 5% in the TTM period compared to 12% three years prior [E27], alongside a severe operational deterioration where debtor days blew out from 77.0 to 116 days [E53]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on sector tailwinds [E62, E64] ignores fundamental reality: a reverse DCF reveals that today's price already aggressively prices in 25.9% earnings growth against a base case of just 6.0% [E43], leaving an extreme DCF overvaluation and a negative margin of safety of -310.0% [E41, E42, E60]. conceded: [E31, E48, E55]
